newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money market trade strained, rates higher.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money market trade strained, rates higher.

text.p: The Croatian money market was strained again on Thursday following a short improvement in liquidity, and term loans were granted at slightly higher rates, dealers said.
"The banks' accounts are experiencing a serious low once again due to regular payments. All of the offer has been exhausted and some 25 million kuna are still sought after," one dealer told Reuters.
The morning trade totalled just 23.8 million kuna, with call money loans granted at an unchanged rate of 10.5 percent, accounting for more than half of the deals.
Due to the market being extremely tight term loans were granted at higher rates than usual.
A 9-day term loan was granted by one savings bank to another at 13.5 percent.

Interbank term loans were given at various higher rates with four-day funds being granted at 11 percent, two-week ones at 14 percent, one-month deals struck at 15 and 16 percent, two-month funds granted at 17 percent and 90-day loans being granted at 18 percent.

Wednesday's overnight trade totalled 82.1 million kuna with two banks seeking funds to cover their shortfalls and one bank needing funds to cover its mandatory reserve. -- Sandra Kalogjera, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
